title: Rust class-group public object adapter
objective: Produce complete ordinary Sage.js conditional-GRH cubic class/unit objects from authenticated Rust publications, including exact arbitrary and fractional ideal witnesses

oracles: Existing ClassUnitComputation and IdealClassGroup proof contracts
exceptions: ADR 0006 permits a qualified handwritten Rust mathematical core while ordinary Python owns public semantics and independent replay

handoff.summary: Rust resident cubic ideal queries now publish a compact exact I/R principal witness, using authenticated Smith lifts plus dense or cached compact relation solves. The Python replay verifies the v1 receipt, exact ideal equalities, relation factors, canonical coordinates, and fractional-ideal denominator normalization, then promotes authenticated publications with an injected resident callback to ordinary complete conditional-GRH IdealClassGroup, UnitGroupComputation, and ClassUnitComputation objects. Analytic replay reuses its exact splitting map, verifies the published BDF bound directly at adaptive rigorous precision, and no longer repeats the expensive minimal-bound search. Focused Python public/presentation tests pass 13/13 and the Rust crate passes 15 library tests, 3 CLI tests, and doctests.
risks: The shared runtime still must wrap its frozen backend.call generation/handle session as the adapter's out-of-band synchronous query_callback; without it the adapter intentionally returns an incomplete computation.
pnpm test:changed stops at the shared number-field-global-arithmetic lazy byte budget (1836688 exceeds 1830000); the integration lane must update the shared package budget or split ownership.
pnpm test:baselib:strict is blocked by pre-existing doubled-backtick docstrings in unclaimed benchmark files on the base branch.
pnpm test:native rebuilt through stage 7/8, then failed because the existing numerical production manifest toolchain identity differs; no lane source failure was reported.
Native validation in this lane was Linux x64 only; integration still owns macOS arm64 and Windows fallback qualification.
next_steps: Integration lane: construct query_callback around backend.call('query', {generation, handle, ...}) and close the resident handle with the frozen capability/open/publication/query/close protocol.
Integration lane: resolve the shared lazy-byte budget and base formatting/toolchain-receipt failures, then rerun test:changed, test:baselib:strict, and test:native.
Run the public row-6 end-to-end path through the actual resident host and exercise arbitrary integral and fractional ideals before release dispatch is enabled.
